full_judgment:
2. On 30.11.1989 the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 307 of 1989 in the Court of Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka against the petitioners and proforma opposite parties praying for a declaration that the election of the Executive Committee of Bangladesh Chalachitra Paribeshak Samity held on 19.11.1989 is illegal, void and without jurisdiction. 

 3. On the same day, i.e. on 30.11.1989, the plaintiff-opposite parties filed an application under Order 39, rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for restraining the defendant-petitioners and others functioning as the Executive Committee of the aforesaid Bangladesh Chalachittra Paribeshak Samity and from taking forcible possession of the office of the said samity. 

 17. A mere perusal of the impugned order shows that the learned Assistant Judge did not apply his judicial mind to the facts and circumstances of the plaintiffs' case, The impugned order does not show that there is a prima facie case in favour of the plaintiffs and there is nothing to show that balance of convenience is in favour of granting the plaintiffs' ad-interim relief. The learned Assistant Judge did not also find that the plaintiffs would suffer an irreparable injury if an order of ad-interim injunction was not passed. 

 19. But m paragraph 6 of the affidavit-in-opposition, the plaintiff-opposite parties have denied the above allegations of the petitioners in the following manner:- 

 "6. That the allegations made in paragraphs 7 to 13 of the revisional application are all false, concocted and cannot be alleged or considered at this stage. The Opposite Parties reserve their right to challenge and controvert all these bogus and false allegations in proper forum. However the opposite parties assert that the allegations that the Election Board was legally constituted or that the election was duly held on 19.11.1989 or that 124 voters cast their votes or that the alleged actions of Ministry of Commerce and the Director of Trade Organisations were legal or that the petitioners have assumed the Office of Executive Committee or that they are functioning as such or that the plaintiffs participated and were defeated in the so-called election, etc., are all false and concocted. The true fact, in short, inter alia, is that the Executive Committee of Bangladesh Chalachitra Paribeshak Samity in its meeting held on 17.11.1989 changed the date of election from 19.11.1989 to 24.12.1989 and that the Director of Trade Organisations under the law has no power or authority to fix the date of the said election." 

 20. It appears from paragraph 6 of the Affidavit-in-opposition that the plaintiff-opposite parties simply denied the petitioners case stating that the alleged election was illegal and the petitioners are not functioning as a duly elected Executive Committee of the aforesaid samity. But the plaintiff-opposite-parties did deny the positive assertions of the petitioners that the Director of Trade Organisation under the Ministry of Commerce, Govt. of Bangladesh vide its Notification No. M. C. T. O-A 36/86/688, dated 30.11.89 duly approved the Executive Committee of which the petitioners are Chairman, Vice-Chairman, Secretary General and members of the Executive committee respectively. 

 22. The plaintiff-opposite parties filed a suit for declaratory decree which is an equitable relief. From the above facts it appears that they did not come with clean hands. It will not be out of place, if I quote an observation of Dorab Patel, J. made in the case of Arts Council of Pakistan-Vs-Reazuddin Pirzada, reported in P. L. D. 1969 Karachi. 349 which reads as follows:- 

 "It is settled law that provided a plaintiff comes to Court with clean hands, he will be entitled to an interim injunction if he shows that he has a prima facie case for the relief he seeks, that the balance of convenience is in favour of granting him interim relief and that irreparable injury will be caused to him if an injunction is not granted."
